Anthology

an-THOL-uh-jee — the root means 'flower'; an anthology is literally a gathering of the best flowers, or writings. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Anthology is a published collection of writings by different authors.

The teacher assigned a poetry anthology featuring works from a dozen different award-winning poets.

Worked Example

An editor spends a year reading thousands of short stories submitted by writers all over the world, then selects the twenty best to be printed together in a single book under one title.

That single book gathering together the best work of many different writers is exactly what an anthology is. Unlike a 'novel,' which is one continuous story by one author, an anthology brings together separate works from separate voices.

How Anthology Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

compilation

compilation: a collection of items gathered from various sources

collection

collection: a group of things gathered together

anthology of works

anthology of works: a published gathering of separate literary pieces

Antonyms

single work

single work: one standalone piece by one author

solo piece

solo piece: a work created by a single individual alone

How Strong Is It? — compilation → anthology → collection

compilation vs. anthology

compilation vs. anthology: Compilation is a broader word than anthology -- a compilation can gather almost anything (songs, videos, statistics), while anthology specifically refers to a curated collection of literary writing.

collection vs. anthology

collection vs. anthology: Collection is even more general than compilation: a collection can be any group of items at all, while an anthology is always a deliberately edited literary collection.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — antho-

root — antho-: flower (Greek anthos; the -o- is the Greek linking vowel)

root — -logy

root — -logy: collection, gathering (from Greek legein, 'to gather, choose'; later also 'study of')

Put it together

Put it together: Greek anthos meant 'flower,' and -logy meant 'a gathering.' An anthology, at its root, is literally 'a gathering of flowers' -- an old poetic image for a collection of the finest, most carefully chosen writings.

Use the root in a new word: chrysanthemum

Use the root in a new word: chrysanthemum: Golden chrysanthemums bloomed along the garden path every autumn.
